text.overview:
The Raptor holds the distinction of being the first Inner Sphere OmniMech ever produced. Designed by Luthien Armor Works as a proof of concept after months of studying Clan OmniMech salvage recovered from the Battle of Luthien in 3052, the twenty-five ton design validated that Inner Sphere engineers could replicate the modular technology that had given the Clans such a decisive advantage during the invasion. The Raptor filled the role of a light reconnaissance and fast strike platform, where its ability to rapidly reconfigure loadouts between missions proved invaluable to Draconis Combine commanders adjusting to the new reality of the Clan threat.

Though initially regarded with skepticism by traditionalists within the DCMS, Luthien Armor Works stood behind the design and eventually won over even its harshest critics. The Raptor became the premier light OmniMech of the Combine, and its prolific production saw it spread beyond Combine borders to become one of the most widely fielded Inner Sphere OmniMechs of its era.
text.capabilities:
The Raptor is built on an Alshain Type KR140 endo steel chassis powered by a weight-saving Omni 175 XL engine, giving the design a top speed of just under 119 kilometers per hour. This speed is the Raptor's primary defense, as three and a half tons of StarSlab/4 armor provides only modest protection against sustained fire. The trade-off is deliberate, maximizing the eleven and a half tons of pod space available for mission-specific loadouts, which represents an impressive proportion of the chassis's total mass.

The Prime configuration reflects a versatile combat philosophy, mounting three LRM-5 launchers for long-range harassment alongside two medium lasers and two small lasers for closer engagements. A pair of machine guns provides anti-infantry capability. This mix allows the Prime to contribute meaningfully at multiple range brackets while maintaining the speed to disengage when outmatched.

With seven distinct factory configurations and additional field variants, the Raptor demonstrates the flexibility that makes OmniMech technology so valued. Loadouts range from pure energy builds for extended operations to electronic warfare packages and even an underwater combat configuration, ensuring the Raptor can be tailored to virtually any light 'Mech mission profile.
text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A is designed for extended operations far from supply lines, mounting two large lasers as its primary armament with three small lasers for close defense. The entirely energy-based loadout eliminates ammunition dependency, allowing the Raptor A to operate independently for prolonged periods without resupply, a critical advantage during deep reconnaissance missions behind enemy lines.
text.battleHistory:
The Raptor's origins trace directly to the Battle of Luthien in January 3052, when the combined defense of the Combine capital against Clan Smoke Jaguar and Clan Nova Cat yielded significant quantities of Clan salvage. Luthien Armor Works engineers studied the captured OmniMech technology intensively, and by May 3052, just months after the battle, the first Raptors walked off the production line at the OmniMech Production Facility on Luthien. The very first units were assigned to the Dragon's Claws for testing, with additional Raptors sent to the Sword of Light, Genyosha, and Ghost regiments for further evaluation.

Acceptance within the DCMS was gradual. Many Combine soldiers, steeped in tradition, were slow to appreciate the advantages of an OmniMech that could swap its weapons between engagements. It took years for the standard Combine soldier to recognize the tactical flexibility the Raptor offered, but its performance during Operation Bulldog in 3059 and the Combine-Dominion War proved decisive in cementing the design's reputation. By the early 3060s, the Raptor was found in the regiments of every top-rated command within the Combine.

The Raptor's success saw it proliferate beyond Combine boundaries, becoming available to allied states and even appearing in mercenary commands. The design's "Easy to Maintain" reputation made it popular with units that lacked dedicated OmniMech maintenance facilities, as the Raptor proved more forgiving of improvised repair work than many of its contemporaries.

Production at Luthien Armor Works continued through the Civil War era, but the facility ceased Raptor production during the Jihad when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien devastated much of the planet's industrial capacity. While LAW survived and eventually resumed other production lines, Raptor manufacturing was not restarted, leaving surviving units increasingly reliant on salvage and aftermarket parts to remain operational.

By the early 3060s, the Raptor was found in the regiments of every top-rated command within the Combine.

The Raptor's success saw it proliferate beyond Combine boundaries, becoming available to allied states and even appearing in mercenary commands. The design's "Easy to Maintain" reputation made it popular with units that lacked dedicated OmniMech maintenance facilities, as the Raptor proved more forgiving of improvised repair work than many of its contemporaries.

Production at Luthien Armor Works continued through the Civil War era, but the facility ceased Raptor production during the Jihad when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien devastated much of the planet's industrial capacity. While LAW survived and eventually resumed other production lines, Raptor manufacturing was not restarted, leaving surviving units increasingly reliant on salvage and aftermarket parts to remain operational.

text.overview:
After the Draconis Combine seized New Avalon in 3146, the AFFS scrambled to find new 'Mech models that could be used to counter the DCMS's advance. While searching through old records, an MIIO team rediscovered the Trapdoor 'Mechs and resurrected them. After retooling the JR7-31 (increasing its weight by ten tons) and negotiating with Clan Sea Fox for manufacturing capabilities, the redesigned Rattlesnake II saw the light of day in 3149.

Developed by the Federated Suns from the original JR7-31 Rattlesnake yet ten tons heavier and built with cutting-edge Clan-spec components, the Rattlesnake II is a heavily armed and armored reconnaissance, ambush, and raiding 'Mech. General Motors produces the design at their New Valencia facility, making it one of the few mixed-tech BattleMechs in regular AFFS service.
text.capabilities:
Like the original, the Rattlesnake II is intended to close on a target quickly, unload its firepower all at once, and move away at the same speed. It relies on medium lasers, two Clan-made extended-range medium lasers, backed up by four standard medium lasers and a Clan-built small laser. With its heavy armor, an electronic-countermeasures suite, and a Myomer Accelerator Signal Circuitry system, the Rattlesnake II is designed to be in the thick of the fighting.

In addition to the ER medium lasers, the RSN-1 carries other Clan-tech components: an XL engine, double-capacity heat sinks, and ferro-fibrous armor. The original design specifications proposed incorporating stealth armor, but integration problems resulted in the use of Clan armor instead. Fourteen Clan-spec double heat sinks keep its heat in check even during sustained engagements.

A MASC system allows for bursts of extra speed on an already fast design, reaching 151 km/h when activated. Combined with a jump capacity of 210 meters and Guardian ECM Suite protection, the Rattlesnake II can engage and disengage at will against most opponents.
text.deployment: The primary Rattlesnake II configuration mounts two Clan ER medium lasers and four standard medium lasers as its main armament, supplemented by a Clan ER small laser. A Guardian ECM Suite provides electronic protection, while MASC allows bursts of speed up to 151 km/h. This configuration represents the resurrection of Project Trapdoor concepts with modern Clan-spec technology.
text.battleHistory:
The Rattlesnake II's history started with a long-forgotten psyops operation against the Draconis Combine. In 3042, after the shock of facing Star League-era BattleMechs during the War of 3039, House Davion's MIIO developed Operation Trapdoor. The brainchild of Dr. Robert Madson, the Rattlesnake carried more firepower and heavier armor than its Jenner inspiration.

The chassis was distributed among AFFS regiments in the Draconis March. For ten years, the Rattlesnake and other Trapdoor models tried to sow confusion among the DCMS, mixing battlefield clashes with planned leaks through news items. Operation Trapdoor was discontinued after around seven years, and only a few Trapdoor 'Mechs survived to the end of the Word of Blake Jihad.

Rumors claim that newly built Rattlesnake IIs are being sent to Combine-occupied worlds to give Federated Suns resistance forces a needed weapon against the occupiers. There are reports that a Combine supply depot on Tsamma was raided by a guerrilla force consisting of Jenners carrying significantly more firepower than normal. The four 'Mechs overwhelmed the Combine Strider and Phoenix Hawk guarding the depot, then destroyed the infantry garrison before escaping into the jungle.

text.overview:
The Rattlesnake BattleMech was created for the Ministry of Information, Intelligence, and Operations by Dr. Robert Madson as part of Project Trapdoor sometime after 3042. It is derived from the Jenner to the point of ultimately being arguably just an upgrade variant of it, sharing the Jenner's JR7 alphanumerical code. The design was an upgrade intended to make use of cutting-edge technology recovered from the Helm Memory Core while outwardly appearing as a standard Jenner.

As part of Project Trapdoor, the Rattlesnakes were deployed with an eye to sowing confusion and uncertainty among Draconis Combine forces. They were also used for MIIO black ops missions requiring plausible deniability. The exact number of Rattlesnakes built is unknown, but even at the height of Trapdoor, no more than twenty to thirty were in use, distributed among Armed Forces of the Federated Suns regiments stationed in the Draconis March.
text.capabilities:
The original JR7-31 Rattlesnake from the 3040s featured cutting-edge technologies including ferro-fibrous armor, an XL engine, and a Guardian ECM Suite. Its main armament consists of seven medium lasers, giving it devastating close-range firepower that far exceeds a standard Jenner. Eleven double heat sinks are only just capable of keeping its heat in check when all weapons fire.

Two additional jump jets were added to the original five, for a total of seven, providing 210 meters of jump capability. The design philosophy emphasized overwhelming firepower delivery, close rapidly, unload all weapons at once, and withdraw at the same speed. The ECM suite provides protection against enemy targeting systems during approach and withdrawal.

As far as can be established, Rattlesnakes were created by refitting existing Jenners rather than being built in a proper factory. Each Rattlesnake was effectively hand-built, with components varying between individual machines. This bespoke construction made field repairs challenging but ensured each machine was optimized for its intended pilot and mission profile.
text.deployment: This custom variant served on Solaris VII in 3084, having been fitted with Clan-grade ER medium lasers, a targeting computer, and an Angel ECM suite. The improved electronics and weapons made it a formidable arena fighter, though its origins as a decades-old intelligence operation 'Mech made it something of a curiosity among Solaris combat enthusiasts.
text.battleHistory:
In 3042, after the shock of facing Star League-era BattleMechs during the War of 3039, House Davion's Ministry of Information, Intelligence, and Operations developed Operation Trapdoor. Using technology recovered from the Helm Memory Core, Trapdoor took established 'Mechs, tore them down, and rebuilt them into radically different machines while mostly retaining the outward appearance of the original. The best-known Trapdoor 'Mech was the JR7-31 Rattlesnake.

For ten years, the Rattlesnake and other Trapdoor models tried to sow confusion among the DCMS and the Internal Security Force, mixing battlefield clashes with planned leaks through news items. One mission which involved the destruction of a Warhawk OmniMech by Rattlesnakes was embellished and published as part of the psyops campaign. As of 3084, the 'Mech was widely regarded as an urban legend.

It is debatable how successful the operation was, but when the Clan Invasion began in 3049, Operation Trapdoor had already been discontinued. The remaining Trapdoor 'Mechs continued to be used under a veil of secrecy, but only a few survived to the end of the Word of Blake Jihad. The design would be resurrected decades later when the Draconis Combine seized New Avalon in 3146.

text.overview: BattleMech aficionado scream-sheets from Solaris VII may have called the Rawhide “a baby Scourge by any other name” and “the Kaiser Cash Grab,” but since leaving the factory floor of Kaiser Systems, the Rawhide has continued to provide solid combat service, proving its detractors wrong.
text.capabilities: The Rawhide is manufactured with some parts from a failed Scourge prototype, along with a great deal of standard materials for ease of construction and cost reduction. Apart from the AES and armor, the Rawhide lacks many of the advanced components and equipment found on BattleMechs produced by Kaiser’s competitors. Rather than detract from its success, the Rawhide’s construction is actually a battlefield and salesfloor perk, making the Rawhide popular with budget-conscious users like mercenaries.:br::br::tab:The Rawhide’s energy weapons and flexible missile pack befit its rugged construction and allow it to deploy far from supply lines. Versatile weapons, movement, and jump capability put it on par with the vaunted Griffin, a centuries-old Lyran favorite.
text.battleHistory: Born in the crucible of combat, the Rawhide was named for a Scourge test pilot who died valiantly defending the Kaiser factory from an AMSC raid in 3134. From this bloody beginning the Rawhide has seen combat across the Coventry, Arcturan, and Donegal fronts in the hands of Lyran and mercenary MechWarriors alike. The Jade Falcons, in particular, have come to loathe the sight of Rawhides hunting down the Clan’s favored light OmniMechs, such as the Eyrie and Spirit.:br::br::tab:In the Ridesein River Valley on Coventry, the defending Seventeenth Arcturan Guards RCT was pressed to the point of collapse by three Falcon Clusters. With the Lyrans entrenched along the valley’s steep sides, the Falcons were forced to dislodge them with concentrated frontal assaults along the flatter valley floor. Between the first and second wave of Falcon attacks, General Ross ordered a small group of Arcturan ’Mechs, including a Rawhide, to scout the Gyrfalcon Galaxy’s next avenue of attack.:br::br::tab:Moving among the trees and small open fields, the Guards made contact with a Nova of the First Falcon Strikers advancing on the Lyran lines. Cut off from retreat by the swift-moving Falcon ’Mechs, an Arcturan lance relayed the enemy’s position to the Seventeenth and formed a defensive circle. The Lyrans stood their ground as the Falcons charged. Autocannon fire from a Lyran Enfield and Uziel swatted jumping Falcon battlesuits out of the sky, while accurate PPC fire from the Rawhide accounted for a Kit Fox. But it wasn’t enough. Elementals ripped the Uziel pilot from her cockpit, while two Falcon Cougars disemboweled the Enfield with heavy laser fire. The last to fall was the battered Rawhide when a Grand Summoner, armor in tatters, shredded its engine with heavy autocannon fire.:br::br::tab:Deep in the Gray Mountains on the world of Loxley, elements of the Fifth Lyran Regulars engaged Jade Falcons from Gamma Galaxy in a series of running battles for control of the valuable factories. As the battle entered its fifth day, a large Falcon force again attacked the main approach to the Norse-Storm factory. Sensing something amiss in the lackluster Falcon assault, First Leutnant Tim Schoeneck rounded up two battered companies and made for the factory’s hidden entrance in the Peria Canyon. Schoeneck’s command exited the factory and was near the edge of the canyon when the Falcons came pouring in. Commanding from his battered Rawhide, Schoeneck and his troops threw themselves into combat. The dry, desert-like conditions turned the battle into a swirling, dusty melee. The mostly-energy weapon outfitted Falcon OmniMechs suffered while Schoeneck’s Rawhide shone. Its reflective armor deflected even more weapons fire than normal as he waded into close combat with a lone Hatchetman at his side. Schoeneck decapitated a Shadow Cat II with an AES-assisted PPC shot and cored a Pinion with laser fire. The Lyrans won the day when he and two Thunder Hawks collapsed a section of canyon on the last Clan ’Mech, a time-honored way to defeat Jade Falcons.
text.notableUnits: Hauptmann Kohl von Grunwald: Kohl von Grunwald was on Tharkad for R&R when his Fourteenth Lyran Guards were destroyed by Clan Wolf, so he joined the reformed Seventeenth Arcturan Guards. On Coventry, his company was alone and cut off in the Ridesein River Valley. Kohl and his Rawhide, Cabbage’s Ride, led the Falcons on a merry chase through the valley for three full days until reconnecting with the Seventeenth. During the chase, Cabbage’s Ride accounted for three Falcon ’Mechs, including a brand-new Ion Sparrow.:br::br:Hauptmann Tim Schoeneck: After proving capable of greater responsibilities in his command of the ad-hoc forces on Loxley after other officers had fallen, Schoeneck was promoted and transferred to the Eleventh Lyran Guards. His expertise in combat reconnaissance will serve the Eleventh well in their border defense against the Wolf Empire.

text.overview:
The Reconquista holds the distinction of being the first BattleMech ever produced by Nueva Castile, a collection of deep periphery worlds that had existed in isolation for centuries before contact with the mysterious Umayyad Caliphate in 2830. Produced by the Asturias Royal BattleMech Yard beginning around 2835, the Reconquista was named as a hopeful symbol of the liberation to come.

A seventy-five-ton primitive design, the Reconquista was crude by any standard, falling far short of even early Inner Sphere designs. Yet, it fulfilled its critical purpose, giving the Castilians their first indigenous BattleMech capability at a time when every 'Mech on the battlefield mattered.
text.capabilities:
The Reconquista is a slow, heavily compromised design born of desperation rather than refined engineering. Its Fury Turbines 180 internal combustion engine propels the seventy-five-ton chassis to a maximum speed of just 32 kilometers per hour, making it one of the slowest 'Mechs ever fielded. This glacial pace left it highly vulnerable to Umayyad artillery and fast-moving armor formations, which could dictate engagement ranges with impunity. The design mounts no jump jets, further limiting its tactical flexibility on any terrain.

The Reconquista's armament proved more successful than its mobility. A single autocannon/10 provides its primary striking power, capable of delivering punishing hits at medium range. A ten-tube long-range missile launcher offers indirect fire support, while a single machine gun provides close-range anti-infantry capability. The Iron Hide Heavy armor gives the design respectable protection for a primitive 'Mech, and its seven heat sinks prove adequate for the relatively modest heat output of its ballistic and missile weapons.

The Reconquista's greatest weakness lay in its components. The ICE engine, myomer bundles, chassis frame, control systems, and software were all plagued by mechanical faults, leading to chronic reliability problems throughout the design's service life. Spare parts shortages only compounded these issues.
text.deployment: No factory variants of the Reconquista are known to have been produced. The Asturias Royal BattleMech Yard manufactured the design in a single configuration throughout its production run, with the Castilian military prioritizing volume over diversification. The 'Mech's primitive construction and limited industrial base made meaningful variant development impractical during the desperate years of the Umayyad conflict. Any battlefield modifications were likely field expedient in nature rather than formalized production variants.
text.battleHistory:
The Reconquista's origin traces to the Umayyad invasion of Nueva Castile in 2830. A single JumpShip carrying armed refugees arrived in the Granada system bearing advanced military technology, including BattleMechs. These invaders, dubbed "Umayyads" by the Castilians after the ancient Islamic empire, quickly conquered several worlds. Their BattleMech superiority proved devastating against the conventional Castilian military, and world after world fell to the technologically superior force.

The tide began to turn when Castilian forces managed to capture an intact Umayyad BattleMech. Combined with intelligence from Umayyad defectors, Castilian engineers at the Asturias Royal BattleMech Yard reverse-engineered the technology and produced the first Reconquista by approximately 2835. While vastly inferior to the Umayyads' Star League-era machines, the Reconquista gave the Castilians their first 'Mech force. By 2841, Reconquistas deployed in company strength were instrumental in halting the Umayyad advance on Valencia. The design's greatest strategic advantage was that it could be manufactured in sufficient numbers at a time when the Umayyads were unable to replace their own 'Mech losses.

Over approximately twenty-five years, the Asturias yard produced nearly two battalions of Reconquistas. Despite chronic mechanical failures and the design's many shortcomings, these 'Mechs formed the backbone of the Castilian counteroffensive that gradually liberated occupied worlds. The Umayyads countered by producing knock-off Korvin tanks, which proved effective enough to prevent a total Castilian victory, but the strategic balance had shifted permanently.

As Castilian industrial capability matured, the Reconquista was eventually phased out in favor of more capable, though still primitive, BattleMech designs. The type largely disappeared from frontline service as Nueva Castile's military technology slowly improved over the following centuries. The long conflict between Nueva Castile and the Umayyad Caliphate ground on until a ceasefire was finally reached after Word of Blake operatives revealed that outside powers had been secretly prolonging the war.

The Reconquista story did not end there, however. When Clan Goliath Scorpion conquered both Nueva Castile and the Umayyad Caliphate, establishing first the Escorpion Imperio and later the Scorpion Empire, some surviving Reconquistas apparently remained in inventory. By 3152, at least one modified Reconquista was reported serving with the Scorpion Conquistadors, a sign of the rugged simplicity of the design, if not its sophistication.

text.overview: The Reptar is a thirty-five-ton light MilitiaMech introduced in 3086 by Quixote Industries for the Escorpión Imperio. Designed by Clan Goliath Scorpion scientists to address the pressing need for military hardware in the Deep Periphery, the Reptar was conceived as a garrison platform to fill the ranks of the Imperio's fledgling military. The design's primary mission is to bolster the conscripted forces assigned to the Scorpion touman and the Imperio's garrison caste, and paired with the heavier Araña MilitiaMech, the Reptar fills the lighter, more mobile role in a two-design tactical partnership that forms the backbone of the Imperio's planetary defense forces.
text.capabilities:
The Reptar's combat capabilities reflect its intended role as a garrison defender rather than a frontline combatant. Powered by a Fuel-EX 175 series fuel cell engine, the design achieves a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour, adequate for patrol duties and rapid redeployment between defensive positions. The fuel cell power plant limits the design's operational endurance compared to fusion-powered machines and constrains its armament to ballistic and conventional weapons. Five tons of Industry-Z Heavy industrial-grade armor provide sufficient protection against the lighter vehicles and infantry formations typical of Deep Periphery adversaries, though the civilian-grade plating would prove wholly inadequate against proper BattleMech weaponry.

The Reptar's armament is built around a Clan ProtoMech AC/8 autocannon mounted in the right arm. This weapon, sourced from surplus ProtoMech production stocks, gives the design surprising firepower for its class at medium ranges. Supplementing the main gun are two Clan light machine guns mounted in the side torsos, providing anti-infantry capability against the foot soldiers and light combatants the Reptar is most likely to encounter. The choice of light machine guns appears unusual for a MilitiaMech of this size, but reflects the Imperio's realistic assessment of the threat environment in the Deep Periphery rather than any aspiration to engage proper military forces on equal terms.
text.deployment: The EPT-C-1 is the sole production model of the Reptar. As a single-configuration design with no factory variants, the EPT-C-1 reflects the Imperio's pragmatic approach to military procurement, fielding a functional garrison platform rather than investing resources in specialized refits for a stopgap design. Reptars are typically paired with the heavier Araña in garrison deployments across the former Nueva Castile territories, where the two designs operate as complementary elements of the Imperio's planetary defense structure.
text.battleHistory:
The Reptar emerged from the upheaval following Clan Goliath Scorpion's absorption of the Nueva Castile worlds in the Deep Periphery during the late Jihad era. The formation of the Escorpión Imperio in the 3080s created an immediate need for military hardware to equip the formerly civilian populations of the conquered territories. With the turmoil engulfing the worlds of Nueva Castile and the competing interests of three regional powers, the Scorpion leadership recognized that even getting one military project from drawing room to production floor was a significant achievement.

Quixote Industries, a local manufacturer, received Clan funding and technology transfers to produce both the Reptar and the Araña MilitiaMechs. The Reptar entered production first in 3086, produced at facilities on Aragon and Navarre, filling a critical gap in the Imperio's garrison forces. Scorpion scientists intended both designs as stopgap measures, equipping the conscripted Castilian and Umayyad freeborns until new Clan-built BattleMech facilities could be completed and brought online.

In observed training exercises, Reptars are typically held back as reserve forces or assigned to protect vital objectives such as command posts and forward observer stations. When Imperio forces require diversionary tactics, Reptar and Araña MilitiaMechs are expected to advance to specified points along an opponent's line, serving as bait to distract or confuse the enemy long enough for superior firepower to arrive. This expendable role reinforces the Scorpion military doctrine's pragmatic view of these designs.

Both MilitiaMech designs have been produced in modest numbers for the Imperio's growing military. With domestic unrest surfacing across several systems, the Reptar has increasingly been deployed for internal security duties, serving as a deterrent against suspected dissident actions among the incorporated populations. Intelligence reports suggest the Reptar was likely replaced in production by the Cazador, a more capable BattleMech design built once Clan manufacturing infrastructure matured.

text.overview: The Rime Otter is a 55-ton medium Clan OmniMech introduced in 3146 by Jötunn BattleWorx for the Rasalhague Dominion. Designed to fill the role of a heavy medium support unit, the Rime Otter was conceived to operate alongside specialist designs within the Dominion's front-line Clusters, providing a rugged anchor for lighter formations or screening heavier assault Stars. Jötunn BattleWorx drew heavily on its experience developing the Grizzly (particularly that design's reinforced internal structure) to create an OmniMech that could absorb punishment far beyond what its weight class would suggest. Built exclusively at the company's facilities on Goito, the Rime Otter represents the Dominion's effort to develop indigenous OmniMech designs rather than relying solely on established Clan Ghost Bear production lines.
text.capabilities:
The Rime Otter is built around a RUFM XL 275 extralight engine augmented by a fixed MASC system, giving it a cruising speed of 54 kph that can be pushed to a sprinting speed of 108 kph in short bursts. This combination allows the design to keep pace with lighter machines such as the Fire Moth while retaining the structural integrity to stand alongside heavier units like the Mastodon. The chassis itself uses a Type 56-55C Modified reinforced internal structure, granting exceptional survivability for a medium OmniMech, the Rime Otter can continue fighting through damage that would cripple less robust designs.

The trade-off for this durability is a relatively modest 18.5 tons of pod space, comparable to many 45-ton designs. This limitation has drawn criticism from MechWarriors who would prefer the firepower of established Sea Fox or WarBear-produced alternatives. IceSheet ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for the weight, while a Garret T10B communications suite and GC Heimdallr System Type 1 targeting system round out the electronics package. The Rime Otter's Prime configuration leans into a brawler role, mounting paired large pulse lasers in the arms alongside an Artemis V-guided LRM-10 with CASE II ammunition protection, a loadout that rewards aggressive pilots willing to close to effective range rather than trade fire at distance.
text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A transforms the Rime Otter into a highly mobile skirmisher through the addition of four jump jets. The primary armament shifts to a right-arm LRM-15 with Artemis V fire control and sixteen volleys of ammunition, providing substantial long-range striking power. A left-arm ER large laser delivers precise fire at extended range, while a Streak SRM-6 launcher with a single ton of ammunition handles close-range engagements. This configuration excels at exploiting terrain through jump mobility, engaging targets at range before repositioning to avoid return fire, a versatile loadout well-suited to the Dominion's combined-arms doctrine.
text.battleHistory:
Rime Otter production began in 3146 at Jötunn BattleWorx on Goito, making it one of the newer OmniMech designs to enter service with the Rasalhague Dominion. The design emerged from the Dominion's broader effort to field indigenous military hardware rather than depending entirely on legacy Clan Ghost Bear production lines or purchases from Clan Sea Fox merchants. Jötunn BattleWorx, already known for the Grizzly, leveraged its experience with reinforced structures to create a medium-weight OmniMech that could serve as the backbone of mixed-weight formations.

The Rime Otter's integration into front-line Clusters proved uneven at first, as warriors accustomed to established designs required time to adapt to the new machine's particular strengths and limitations. Early deployments revealed that some units struggled to employ the design effectively. On Ganshoren, the 300th Battle Cluster's encounter with the Second Falcon Dragoons nearly ended in disaster when warriors used their Rime Otters as shields for Mad Dog Mk III fire-support units, absorbing punishing fire in a role better suited to dedicated heavy 'Mechs. text.overview: The Savage Coyote was developed by Clan Coyote beginning in 3052 following the election of Khan Sullivan Koga, who championed a sweeping modernization of the Clan's military hardware. First fielded in 3059, the 85-ton OmniMech was conceived as a showcase for the Advanced Tactical Missile system, one of Clan Coyote's most significant technological achievements. As the inventors of the OmniMech concept itself, Clan Coyote had seen its influence wane during the decades preceding the Clan Invasion, and the Savage Coyote represented a deliberate effort to revitalize the Clan's military prestige. The assault-weight chassis devotes an exceptional proportion of its mass to modular pod space, giving it unmatched flexibility among Coyote OmniMechs of the era.
text.capabilities:
The Savage Coyote was designed as a true assault platform, with its extra-light engine enabling an unprecedented forty-five tons of pod space, more than half the chassis's total mass dedicated to interchangeable weaponry. This massive payload capacity allows field commanders to configure the 'Mech for virtually any combat role, from long-range fire support to devastating close-quarters brawling. The fifteen tons of Forging ZK11 standard armor provide solid protection for an assault-class OmniMech, though the reliance on an extra-light engine creates a vulnerability to critical torso damage that MechWarriors must account for in combat.

The primary configuration exemplifies the design's emphasis on versatility, pairing two ATM-12 launchers with an ER PPC and an LB 10-X autocannon to maintain effective firepower across all engagement ranges. A complement of ER medium and small lasers provides additional close-range punch. Heat management requires careful discipline, as the fourteen fixed double heat sinks and three additional pod-mounted sinks can be overtaxed when firing all weapons simultaneously. The chassis's cruising speed of 32 kph is modest even by assault 'Mech standards, making the Savage Coyote dependent on its firepower and armor rather than mobility to dominate the battlefield.
text.deployment: The first alternate configuration transforms the Savage Coyote into a mobile close-range combatant, an unusual role for an 85-ton chassis. Jump jets provide up to ninety meters of tactical mobility, allowing the 'Mech to close rapidly with opponents or exploit terrain advantages. A Gauss rifle and ER large laser maintain long-range threat capability during the approach, while three ATM-6 launchers and three medium pulse lasers deliver devastating firepower at short range. An anti-missile system provides additional protection against incoming missile fire, complementing the aggressive close-quarters doctrine this configuration was designed to support.
text.battleHistory:
The Savage Coyote emerged from a period of institutional crisis within Clan Coyote. Despite their historical distinction as the inventors of the OmniMech, the Coyotes had experienced decades of declining political and military influence among the Clans by the mid-thirty-first century. The election of Khan Sullivan Koga in 3052 marked a turning point, as the new Khan directed the Clan's scientist caste to undertake an aggressive modernization program aimed at restoring Coyote prestige.

The development of Advanced Tactical Missile technology proved central to this effort, and the Savage Coyote was designed specifically to showcase this new weapons system. First deployed in 3059, the OmniMech was rushed into mass production across Clan Coyote's industrial base. Every primary 'Mech production facility (Landen on Tamaron, Picuris on Londerholm, and Zuni on Foster) was retooled to manufacture the design, with only the Ashton plant continuing to produce the Canis and Rabid Coyote.

The Savage Coyote quickly became a cornerstone of Coyote military power. Every front-line Cluster fielded multiple examples, and the design's versatility made it valuable across the full spectrum of Clan Coyote operations during the late Civil War era. The 'Mech also attracted the attention of rival Clans, and captured Savage Coyotes appeared in the toumans of several Homeworld Clans, including Clan Star Adder and Clan Cloud Cobra.

The Wars of Reaving brought significant upheaval to Savage Coyote production. The Zuni plant on Foster changed hands during the conflict, falling under Clan Goliath Scorpion control during the Jihad before ultimately passing to Clan Cloud Cobra, which reactivated production at the facility. The Landen and Picuris facilities on Tamaron and Londerholm respectively remained under Coyote control through the Jihad and into the early Dark Age, continuing to produce the chassis for Coyote forces.

By the late Dark Age era, the political instability of the Homeworld Clans had cast uncertainty over the long-term future of these production lines, though the Savage Coyote itself remained a respected and feared design wherever it appeared on the battlefield.

text.overview:
The Scorpion was introduced in 2570 by Brigadier Corporation as one of the earliest quadrupedal BattleMechs to enter active service. Though the Xanthos was actually designed four years earlier, the Scorpion reached the battlefield first, becoming a pioneering design in four-legged 'Mech development. Created by Dr. David Harrison, who had been extracted from Hollis Incorporated following the troubled Xanthos project, the Scorpion was envisioned as a stable weapons platform that would revolutionize 'Mech combat through its unique configuration.

Despite Harrison's optimistic predictions, the Scorpion was received poorly by MechWarriors who found the quad gait's rough ride nearly unbearable. The design became synonymous with undesirable postings, often serving as the last assignment before a pilot faced dispossession or forced retirement. Brigadier ceased primary production before the Succession Wars began, and the Scorpion faded into obscurity for centuries until Defiance Industries' Project Phoenix revival and subsequent upgrades by various manufacturers rehabilitated the design's reputation.
text.capabilities:
The quadrupedal Scorpion is built on a Brigadier 800F chassis powered by a VOX 330 fusion engine, providing a top speed of 97 kilometers per hour. While Dr. Harrison theorized that four-legged 'Mechs would provide superior stability, the ride is notoriously rough, with documented discomfort at cruising speeds between 61 and 65 kilometers per hour. The design carries seven tons of StarSlab armor, providing adequate protection for a medium 'Mech.

The original armament centers on an Anderson Armaments PPC as the primary weapon, which combined with the Scorpion's inherently stable quad chassis makes the 'Mech effective at delivering accurate fire at range. A Marvel Six-Load SRM-6 launcher provides close-range firepower to exploit armor breaches. However, the massive reactor leaves minimal room for protection, and the ammunition bin's exposed position on the left side creates a dangerous vulnerability.

The quad configuration brings inherent trade-offs. While the low-slung profile offers advantages in certain terrain, torso-mounted weapons suffer from limited firing arcs. The Scorpion is particularly vulnerable in urban environments where infantry and vehicles can exploit its arc limitations. Later variants addressed these concerns through suspension redesigns derived from the failed Scorpion LAM project.
text.deployment: This configuration became synonymous with MechWarrior Wendall Puritan II of Smithson's Chinese Bandits, though the modification was actually common during the Third Succession War. When Puritan's Anderson Armaments PPC failed, he was unable to source a replacement, the weapon being more valuable than the Scorpion itself during this era of technological decline. The large laser substitution and additional armor became a widespread field modification for pilots who could not maintain the original weapon system.
text.battleHistory:
Brigadier Corporation began as a contract manufacturer for the Terran Hegemony, building components and systems for other companies' designs. Seeking to establish themselves in the lucrative BattleMech market, Brigadier's board recruited Dr. David Harrison from Hollis Incorporated, where he had been embroiled in the troubled Xanthos quad 'Mech project. Freed from bureaucratic constraints and armed with lessons learned from the Xanthos failures, Harrison brought his dream of a four-legged combat 'Mech to fruition in 2570. Despite his predictions that the Scorpion would revolutionize warfare, the design received little praise outside the company.

The Scorpion quickly developed a reputation as a punishment posting. Poor sales led Brigadier to cease manufacturing before the Succession Wars began, and the design faded from prominence. During the Third Succession War, the few remaining Scorpions became increasingly difficult to maintain. The Anderson Armaments PPC proved more valuable than the 'Mech itself, leading many pilots to replace the particle cannon with large lasers when original weapons failed. By the mid-3020s, the Lyran Commonwealth had begun cannibalizing their Scorpions for parts, a process the Federated Suns accelerated following the War of 3039.

The 2925 battle between the Fusiliers of Oriente and the Liao Guard marked a notable moment in Scorpion history, serving as the final action of the Sixth Liao Guards before their disbandment. Heavy fighting on Hesperus II in 3065 uncovered a long-forgotten bunker containing records and prototypes from an abandoned Scorpion LAM program. While Defiance Industries had no interest in reviving the failed LAM concept, the chassis redesign data promised to correct the handling issues that had plagued the Scorpion for centuries.

The success of other quad designs like the Tarantula and Barghest convinced Defiance to license production rights from Brigadier and develop the SCP-12S variant. Meanwhile, Word of Blake representatives approached Brigadier directly in 3067, commissioning the SCP-12C for their expanding military. The Blakists' reconstruction of Oliver's factories enabled production of additional variants including the SCP-10M. During the Jihad, Scorpions played a notable role in the resistance on Terra Firma, where partisan forces centered around lances of the quad 'Mechs ambushed Word of Blake forces with devastating effectiveness.

Following Gray Monday, Brigadier reintroduced a classic Scorpion design based heavily on templates developed by the small refit outfit Bander BattleMechs, which had spent years correcting the original's design flaws. The new variants found popularity with militias, mercenaries, and Republic splinter groups including Bannson's Raiders. When Clan Wolf invaded Oliver, the defending Scorpions proved less successful against frontline OmniMechs, and the facility's capture left Bander BattleMechs on Terra Firma as the sole Inner Sphere source for the design. The Wolves have since kept limited production of Brigadier Scorpions, upgrading them with Clan technology to create the fearsome Scorpion C variant.

text.overview: The Scourge is a 65-ton heavy BattleMech designed by Kaiser Systems on the Lyran world of Herzberg, first reaching production lines in 3131 using proven, readily available technology. An improved model incorporating advanced components followed two years later, enhancing combat performance while maintaining the same proven chassis. Conceived as a versatile general-purpose combatant equally capable of operating as a heavy scout, the Scourge fills a valuable niche between dedicated reconnaissance platforms and frontline assault units. Kaiser Systems licensed production to StarCorps Industries, significantly expanding availability beyond Lyran space. The relatively recent introduction of the Scourge means many opponents encounter it without prior knowledge of its capabilities, granting pilots a notable tactical advantage through unfamiliarity.
text.capabilities:
Built on Kaiser's Quadriga I endo steel frame and powered by a VOX 325 XL engine, the Scourge achieves a top speed of 86 kilometers per hour, well above average for a 65-ton heavy 'Mech. Four Dynamo jump jets provide 120 meters of jump capability, granting the design exceptional tactical flexibility for its weight class. The 'Mech's combat profile draws comparisons to venerable designs like the Shadow Hawk and Vindicator in its ability to serve multiple battlefield functions.

The Scourge's primary armament centers on an Eisen Gauss rifle mounted in the left arm, delivering devastating long-range firepower. A quartet of Diverse Optics extended range medium lasers in the right arm provides potent close-range punch, enhanced in the WF1 model by an actuator enhancement system that yields exceptional accuracy. A single medium pulse laser in the left arm rounds out the weapons loadout. Durallex super light ferro-fibrous armor on the advanced model provides solid protection while keeping tonnage available for the weapons payload.

The design's principal limitation lies in its Gauss rifle ammunition supply. With only sixteen rounds available, sustained engagements can quickly deplete the Scourge's primary weapon, forcing pilots to rely on their laser array for continued combat effectiveness.
text.deployment: This variant was an experimental prototype developed at Kaiser Systems on Herzberg beginning in 3132. This radical modification replaced the standard Gauss rifle with a Clan-specification Ultra autocannon/10 and improved heavy large laser in the left arm, while mounting reflective armor and a heavy-duty gyro for enhanced survivability. Three Clan-specification extended range medium lasers and an actuator enhancement system occupied the right arm. The design sacrificed jump capability entirely to accommodate the heavier equipment. Chronic technical problems, including cascading software conflicts and an uncontrollable arm twitch caused by overloaded actuator systems, prevented the WX1 from leaving the test hangar. The sole prototype was destroyed during an Eighth Free Worlds Guards raid on Herzberg in 3134, and the concept was not pursued further.
text.battleHistory:
The Scourge emerged during a period of considerable upheaval in the Inner Sphere, entering service as the Blackout severed HPG communications across human-occupied space. Kaiser Systems, an established manufacturer on Herzberg, developed the design to meet the Lyran Commonwealth's growing need for versatile heavy BattleMechs capable of independent operations. The initial SCG-WD1 model reached production in 3131, using proven components that could be sourced reliably despite disrupted supply chains.

Recognizing the design's potential, Kaiser Systems licensed production to StarCorps Industries, which brought its facilities on Emris IV and Loburg online to produce the Scourge. This arrangement significantly increased production capacity and, through the Emris IV plant's location within the former Free Worlds League, expanded the design's reach beyond Lyran space. The advanced SCG-WF1 entered production in 3133, offering enhanced combat performance through advanced armor and improved targeting systems, though its reliance on advanced components restricted production volume compared to the more accessible WD1.

Kaiser Systems also explored more radical modifications during this period. An experimental prototype designated SCG-WX1 attempted to integrate Clan-specification weaponry and reflective armor into the Scourge chassis beginning in 3132. Persistent technical difficulties kept the prototype confined to Kaiser's test hangar. The sole WX1 was ultimately destroyed defending the factory complex during an Eighth Free Worlds Guards raid on Herzberg in 3134, ending the experimental program.

By 3136, the Scourge had established itself in Lyran service, seeing action against raiding forces throughout the Commonwealth's border regions. A militia garrison on Wiltshire employed a Scourge to devastating effect against raiding elements of Able's Aces that year, demonstrating the design's effectiveness in defensive operations against numerically superior light forces. The pirate-hunting mercenary Wrathful Privateers adopted Scourges as lance leaders in their scout company by 3140, successfully tracking raiders across Lyran worlds. These engagements underscored the Scourge's suitability for independent scouting operations, where its combination of speed, firepower, and durability allowed it to operate effectively ahead of supporting forces.

Export sales of the SCG-WD1 have spread the design to mercenary commands and smaller realms throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery, though the advanced WF1 remains concentrated in Lyran and Free Worlds League service. The Scourge continues to see expanding adoption as commanders recognize its versatility in an era defined by disrupted communications and decentralized operations.
